sentences.text: Revenue moved from $41.9 billion in FY2016 to $47.9 billion in FY2025, a 1.5% CAGR [F1][F10][F219].
The window is not a compounder but a refranchising story: revenue fell 13.5% in FY2017 and 5.3% in FY2018 [D42][D93], then recovered 17.1% in FY2021 and 11.3% in FY2022 [D246][D297].
The FY2017 decline came with a 42.8% drop in Bottling Investments revenue as bottling operations were refranchised [D572][P71].

FY2025 operating income jumped 37.7% to $13.8 billion [D450][F40], which the filing attributes to lower other operating charges after the prior-year fairlife contingent-consideration remeasurement, concentrate volume growth of 1% and favorable pricing [P12].
Concentrate operations supplied 59.4% of FY2025 revenue and 1.6pp of its 1.9% growth [D532][D534][D449], while finished product operations added 0.3pp [D541].
By geography, the United States contributed 1.6pp of FY2025 growth on a 39.9% revenue share, against 0.2pp from non-US markets [D525][D523][D484].
Operating costs grew 9.7pp slower than revenue in FY2025 [D474], and operating income grew 37.7% against revenue growth of 1.9% [D450][D449].
Net income grew 23.3% and diluted EPS 23.6% in FY2025 [D451][D453], with the diluted share count down 0.2% [D468].
Over the window net income compounded at 8.1% against revenue's 1.5% [F222][F219], and EPS basic matched net income at 8.1% [F223].
FY2025 operating margin of 28.7% is the window high, above the 26.0% median and the 20.7% low [F50][D765][D766][D764].
Gross margin rose 0.6pp to 61.6%, above its 60.7% window median [F30][D462][D772].

The FY2025 operating-margin gain of 7.5pp [D463] came mostly from the 6.2pp residual other-lines effect [D477], which the filing ties to lower other operating charges after the prior-year fairlife remeasurement [P12].
In FY2025 net margin of 27.3% sat 1.4pp below the 28.7% operating margin [F70][F50][D810], with a 17.9% effective tax rate [D435].
Operating cash flow of $7.4 billion was 0.57x net income in FY2025, the window low against a 1.18x median [F100][D436][D799][D800].
Free cash flow of $5.3 billion was 0.40x net income, also the window low against a 0.97x median [F120][D437][D776][D778].
The FY2024 collapse to 0.64x [D386] was driven primarily by the $6.0 billion IRS Tax Litigation Deposit [P22].
Capex of $2.1 billion was 4.4% of revenue and 2.01x D&A [F110][D432][D438], and free cash flow margin of 11.0% sits below the 20.2% window median [D433][D775].
Cash and investments were $10.3 billion at FY2025 [D440], and the pack's net-cash series stops at FY2023, when net debt was $32.4 billion, -70.7% of revenue [D341][D342].
The current ratio of 1.46x is the window high against a 1.13x median [F200][D780][D781].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.5 billion were 179.9% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D444][D445], and the diluted share count fell 0.2% [D468].
Payout above free cash flow for three straight years means the dividend is being funded partly from the balance sheet rather than current cash generation [D344][D395][D445].

Revenue for FY2017 and FY2018 in the table is a later recast, $36.2 billion and $34.3 billion against $35.4 billion and $31.9 billion first reported [F2][X2][F3][X3], so growth spanning those years mixes presentations [R1].
The recast makes the FY2017-FY2018 revenue declines and the FY2019 rebound unreliable as a read on underlying demand [R1].
Long-term debt is not reported after FY2023 [X194], so net cash and debt growth after that omit it [R9].
The missing debt line means the FY2025 leverage picture cannot be read from this pack [R9].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2024 and FY2025, at 0.45x and 0.40x [D387][D437][R3].
Two years of weak conversion against a 0.97x median is the most persistent operating concern here [D778][R3].
Whether operating cash flow to net income recovers above the 1.18x window median from 0.57x in FY2025 [D436][D800], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether operating margin holds above the 26.0% window median after the 28.7% FY2025 high [F50][D766], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether buybacks plus dividends fall back below the 105.1% FY2023 level from 179.9% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D445][D344], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
